name: A dry, caffeine-free nonbeer drink for a whole social evening
proposition: An adult, less-sweet drink that remains pleasant over a long dinner, games night or pub visit when choosing no alcohol.
target_customer_occasion_geography: Czech adults who dislike beer and sweet mocktails; initially Prague/Brno independent hospitality plus take-home. German urban secondary comparison, not assumed common segment. Recurring evening gatherings; precise frequency unknown.
substitutes_unresolved_need: AF beer, Mattoni RTD, Crodino, tonic, zero cola, kombucha and water. Hypothesised unresolved combination is low perceived sweetness, no caffeine, nonbeer flavour and affordable multiple serves—not basic availability.
need_evidence: Topic 05 Czech self-reports and French exploratory discussion; category social participation evidence. No representative Czech measurement of this particular segment.
paid_demand_evidence: Existing CZ retailer offers and opaque repeat badges, especially Crodino, support some paid use; no willingness to pay for extra dryness or startup premium.
competitors_differentiation: Mattoni G&T has 4 g sugar/100 ml and CZK 19.90 makes price-led mocktail imitation weak; Crodino has higher labelled sugar (15 g/100 ml), but perceived sweetness was not tested and depends on acidity, bitterness and serving conditions. Must win perceived dryness/length of drinking, not claim everyone dislikes sweetness.
format_experience: Conceptual 330 ml can or 330–500 ml bottle, controlled carbonation, citrus/herb/bitter profile using ordinary food preparations. Format a test variable; no recipe validated.
promise_science_claims_classification: Social tonic; sensory/participation benefit, no physiological relaxation promise. Enjoyment/occasion only. Ordinary beverage classification most plausible; less-sweet is sensory descriptor, “low sugar” only if legal nutrient threshold met and lab confirmed. No “reduces stress”, “social buzz” or driving-safety efficacy claim.
repeat_pattern: Preferred flavour/participation during the next gathering, potentially multiple servings. Need proof of second-serving liking and total-evening spend; no recommended dose.
price_channel_benchmarks: CZK 19.90/330 ml Mattoni promo, 24.90 reference; CZK 59.97/175 ml Crodino; CZK 19.90/500 ml Birell inherited. Independent venues/retailer mixed baskets reduce single-order liquid delivery burden. No target price decided.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: Multiple-serving ingredient review, exact ABV verification, bitterness/astringency/sweetener aftertaste, can lining/acid compatibility, pasteurization and ambient shelf life. Conventional formulation likely simpler than sedative extracts; quotation/MOQ unknown here.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: Cheap domestic incumbents plus improving AF beer; satisfied cola/water drinkers. The niche may be small, and sweetener-free dryness may taste thin or harsh.
invalidating_assumptions: Preference disappears at economically viable price; only novelty trials; customers choose cheaper beer/Mattoni; venues lack repeat orders.
cheapest_next_validation: Before any development spend, a structured comparison of existing real alternatives with target-segment occasion/receipt diaries and a paper choice exercise including total-evening cost. No tests conducted. Subsequent controlled sensory/preorder work requires a separately authorised protocol; do not sell an unvalidated formula.
need_evidence_strength: Documented adjacent occasion; specific combined need exploratory
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: No new-product willingness to pay or verified repeat
occasion_frequency_breadth: Recurring evenings plausible; frequency and segment size unknown
competitive_defensibility: Weak until perceived sensory advantage and route established; strong cheap substitutes
regulatory_feasibility: Ordinary conventional beverage comparatively plausible; final preparations/label unknown
scientific_credibility: Sensory proposition; no physiological effect required
manufacturing_capital: Relatively simpler formulation; compatible pack and MOQ/cost unknown
channel_economics: Independent venues/mixed baskets plausible; access and contribution unknown
assumption_dependence: High: dissatisfied segment, second-serving liking, total-evening spend
recommendation: First social learning priority; no development/production commitment
report_section: A dry, caffeine-free nonbeer drink for a whole social evening

name: A small dinner-pairing bottle for the only non-drinker at the table
proposition: A ready-to-pour adult drink matched to food, with enough complexity for dinner and a portion that does not require opening a 750 ml bottle for one person.
target_customer_occasion_geography: French urban diners/hosts choosing AF while companions drink wine; NL specialty food/hospitality secondary test. Restaurant dinner or weekend hosting, frequency unmeasured.
substitutes_unresolved_need: Water, soda, AF wine/beer, sparkling tea, made-to-order mocktails. Hypothesis is small-format food pairing and low wastage/commitment, not absence of sophisticated alcohol-free options.
need_evidence: IFOP variety demand, exploratory small-bottle comment, existing premium gastronomic positioning; specific portion dissatisfaction remains weak evidence.
paid_demand_evidence: French domestic Copenhagen 750 ml at EUR 25.50 listings show a price on offer; no verified selling volume/repeat or small-bottle premium acceptance.
competitors_differentiation: Copenhagen Sparkling Tea, Symples 330 ml, Yoleau 250 ml, AF wine and kombucha. Portion alone is copyable; need a proven food/sensory fit plus venue access.
format_experience: 250–330 ml glass single dinner serving or 375 ml for two; tea/verjus/culinary botanical direction, still or light sparkle; no validated recipe, caffeine must be measured if tea used.
promise_science_claims_classification: Social tonic; gastronomic/social, no functional efficacy core. Food pairing and sensory description; ordinary beverage plausible, not a supplement. Exact botanical preparations, residual alcohol and labelling still require review.
repeat_pattern: Reorder with familiar meal or venue; small size reduces leftover commitment. Whether frequency covers packaging costs unknown.
price_channel_benchmarks: Copenhagen 750 ml at €25.50 retail; Symples 330 ml at €2.75; Yoleau 3×250 ml at €6.49; use food shops, restaurants and grocery mixed baskets. No assumed restaurant margin or customer price ceiling.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: Tea haze/astringency, oxygen/light, micro control and glass freight; portion packaging economics; restaurant refrigeration/menu turnover and distributor terms; no guaranteed startup MOQ.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: Existing single-serve mocktails/herbal drinks already solve portion; restaurant pour-by-glass can solve 750 ml waste. Wine imitation may disappoint; lower opening volume raises unit packaging costs.
invalidating_assumptions: Diners prefer water or existing brands; no repeat venue demand; consumers treat it as rare celebration; flavour preference not stable across dishes.
cheapest_next_validation: Desk-audit menus/retailer small formats and public reviews for genuine portion complaints, then authorised structured customer/venue research comparing full bottle, by-glass and single portion; do not assume a bottle problem from one comment.
need_evidence_strength: Stated variety encouragement; portion-specific need very weak
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: Premium offers only; no verified volume/paid premium/repeat
occasion_frequency_breadth: Dinner/hosting recurrent in principle; exact cadence unknown
competitive_defensibility: Existing small formats and by-glass service; no defensibility shown
regulatory_feasibility: Ordinary tea/food route plausible; exact preparation/caffeine/ABV review
manufacturing_capital: Tea stability and glass packaging add cost; MOQ unknown
channel_economics: Restaurants/food retail fit; access, waste savings and margins unknown
assumption_dependence: High: portion dissatisfaction and food preference at viable price
report_section: A small dinner-pairing bottle for the only non-drinker at the table

name: A chilled weekday “day is done” ritual without an efficacy promise
proposition: A ready-to-open evening drink that marks stopping work and replaces the habit of an alcoholic first drink.
target_customer_occasion_geography: German/French adults reducing weekday drinking at home; optional Czech pilot only if demand shown. Potentially several weekdays, not measured.
substitutes_unresolved_need: Tea, water, AF beer, Symples Relax, Neuroblends RELAX, kombucha and ordinary soft drinks. Hypothesised unmet convenience/ritual, not established lack of supply.
need_evidence: Repository public evening voices; established calm-positioned products. No representative frequency/purchase study of this exact problem.
paid_demand_evidence: Neuroblends 24×330 ml at €64.90 and Symples 330 ml at €2.75 offers; subscription button not proof retention. US experience cannot validate EU purchase.
competitors_differentiation: Symples already close; Neuroblends adds actives. Differentiate only through demonstrated preferred experience/ritual. A claim-free formula may be safer but commercial differentiation weaker.
format_experience: 250–330 ml chilled can/bottle; aromatic food-use infusion, low sweetness, no caffeine; conceptual.
promise_science_claims_classification: Social tonic (unwind occasion), not a sleep supplement. Sensory pause, not anxiolysis/sedation/sleep improvement; ordinary beverage plausible. No clinical effect assumed; strong therapeutic framing would undermine category choice.
repeat_pattern: Pleasant stopping-work cue; purchasing must survive absence of a noticeable psychoactive effect. Ritual can also be served by cheap tea.
price_channel_benchmarks: EUR 2.70/can Neuroblends 24-pack; EUR 2.75 Symples retail; specialty grocery or mixed case, not assumed profitable single-can DTC.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: Food-use botanical preparation; taste/stability; honest wording; shipping pack weight; no multi-can sedating actives; exact label review.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: Existing supply already fits; premium drink might be rejected without promised feeling, as exploratory US Hiyo voices show. Need may be fulfilled free by changing routine.
invalidating_assumptions: No paid repeat without efficacy narrative; consumers prefer warm tea or reducing liquid at night; unit economics require unjustified premium.
cheapest_next_validation: Future diary/receipt study with current beverages and explicit no-efficacy positioning before formula development. No recruitment or study was performed.
need_evidence_strength: Exploratory ritual accounts; specific unmet need weak
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: Offers only; no new paid-repeat evidence
competitive_defensibility: Very close existing Symples/Neuroblends and cheap tea
regulatory_feasibility: Ordinary food infusion plausible without efficacy promises
scientific_credibility: No clinical effect established or required for ritual
manufacturing_capital: Simple formula possible; botanical specs/ambient stability unresolved
channel_economics: Specialty mixed basket plausible; DTC delivery and acquisition unknown
assumption_dependence: High: willingness to pay without felt effect
report_section: A chilled weekday “day is done” ritual without an efficacy promise

name: A clearly portioned early-afternoon drink where coffee and full-strength energy are poor fits
proposition: a pleasant chilled drink with an explicitly modest, predictable caffeine portion for an early-afternoon work break.
target_customer_occasion_geography: adults already buying drinks for the lunch-to-work transition; Czech urban workplaces/coworking first research cell, Polish equivalent as a comparison, contingent on founder access. Occurrence could be multiple weekdays, but actual segment frequency is unknown.
substitutes_unresolved_need: free coffee, smaller coffee, tea, cola, CANS+, Vilgain/Olimp, water and a walk. Possible gap is convenient cold availability plus preferred flavour/portion, not absent caffeine supply. It remains unproven that alternatives are inadequate.
need_evidence: repository Czech/English exploratory accounts distinguish caffeine avoidance, overstimulation and the break itself. EFSA states some adults' sleep is affected by 100 mg near bedtime; this supports careful timing and dose transparency, not a promise that a lower amount is sleep-safe. [Customer evidence](../../research/customers/05-segments-and-occasions/supporting/work-focus-evidence.md); [EFSA](https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en/topics/topic/caffeine).
paid_demand_evidence: exact local competing offers establish a functioning supply and plausible price reference; neither our target's willingness to pay nor repeat exists. Neutonic is an external UK/global signal, not local validation.
competitors_differentiation: CANS+ at 42.24 mg is exceptionally close; a new formula alone has no defensible difference. A specific workplace route, sensory preference and transparent whole-can dose might differentiate if users/payors confirm it. No exclusive venue or route is secured.
format_experience: one 250–330 ml can or bottle, tea/fruit flavour and controlled sweetness; no validated recipe. No caffeine dose is selected. A 40–60 mg preference concept would need separate evaluation and cannot inherit the evidence supporting alertness at at least 75 mg.
promise_science_claims_classification: functional supplement drink commercially; likely ordinary beverage if simple beverage ingredients/presentation, not automatically a supplement. modest caffeine delivery, with no promise of more completed work or “no crash.” Ingredient caffeine evidence is much stronger than evidence for a proprietary blend. A 21-person randomized caffeine-matched beverage study found no significant between-condition advantage on tested outcomes; it does not prove all blends ineffective. EFSA specifically found the proposed alertness relationship unsubstantiated at 40–less than 75 mg in its 2014 assessment. This is a material limitation for transferring that assessment to a modest-dose concept, not proof that every lower dose is ineffective. A later randomised study reported attention/alertness improvements at 60 mg in 82 healthy adults aged 40–60 with low/nonhabitual caffeine intake; the narrow population, tested delivery and company-affiliated authors limit transfer to this unformulated drink. It does not change claim authorisation or establish work productivity. [Wilhelmus et al., published online September 2016; 2017 issue](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27649778/). Evidence at at least 75 mg still does not create an authorised claim. [EFSA 2014 opinion](https://www.efsa.europa.eu/en/efsajournal/pub/3574). Claims need current jurisdictional assessment. [Pereira et al., 2024](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39257647/).
repeat_pattern: taste/convenience at a recurring work break, one portion replacing an existing purchase, not encouraged stacking. Frequency and number of paid weeks are unknown.
price_channel_benchmarks: 39.50–45 CZK/330 ml Czech retail; PLN 4.99 Polish focus can; offices, coworking cafés, small convenience outlets before freight-heavy single-can DTC.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: country/label review, caffeine and total intake instructions, stable flavour and dose, process/pack compatibility, local wholesale contribution and secured trial outlet. Published co-packer minima from topic 12 are not offers for this recipe.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: CANS+ already fits the thesis, free coffee is strong, dissatisfaction may concern overwork rather than drinks, and lower caffeine may feel insufficient. The apparent access gap may vanish in a local outlet audit.
invalidating_assumptions: few genuinely dissatisfied frequent buyers; only “stronger focus” copy wins; acceptable price falls below landed contribution; identical existing product is readily available; employer is the payor and refuses.
cheapest_next_validation: first a local shelf/menu/office-offer audit against CANS+ and ordinary tea/coffee, followed (only in future separately authorised fieldwork) by recent-purchase interviews with explicit no-purchase and existing-brand options. Kill before formulation if no repeated unsatisfactory paid occasion is identifiable.
need_evidence_strength: Familiar work-break habit; unmet need weak
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: Competing offers; no new-product cohort or premium evidence
competitive_defensibility: CANS42.24 mg and office offer directly challenge; no secured access
regulatory_feasibility: Ordinary caffeinated beverage plausible; national dose/category and claims constraints
scientific_credibility: Caffeine general mechanism; 60 mg narrow trial; final dose/matrix unresolved; no automatic authorised claim
manufacturing_capital: Conventional route plausible; 250 ml and 330 ml supplier fit differ; quote unknown
channel_economics: Workplaces/cafes potential; user/payor and free alternatives decisive
assumption_dependence: High: distinct dissatisfied buyer, dose/experience, accessible profitable route
recommendation: Conditional functional learning priority only; no production commitment
report_section: A clearly portioned early-afternoon drink where coffee and full-strength energy are poor fits

name: A caffeine-free nutrition drink for the afternoon pause, for existing magnesium-supplement users
proposition: make a chosen magnesium/nutrient routine convenient in a pleasant drink during an afternoon pause; do not promise immediate calm.
target_customer_occasion_geography: adults already using magnesium supplements who dislike tablets/preparation, Czechia or Germany as separate initial cells; daily routine frequency is hypothetical until observed.
substitutes_unresolved_need: tablets, powders, mineral water, CANS+ Balance, Magnesia Antistress, Biolectra liquid, herbal tea. Need would be convenience, taste and replacement of an existing routine; dissatisfaction with tablets in this exact customer group is not yet documented.
need_evidence: topic 05 finds caffeine-free pause interest and ritual needs; this is adjacent rather than direct evidence for nutrient-routine replacement. Existing liquid-dose products show feasible format supply, not unmet need. [Biolectra](https://www.biolectra-magnesium.de/produkte/biolectra-magnesium-300-mg-liquid/).
paid_demand_evidence: exact price/stock offers exist, but no finished-drink repeat, convenience premium or switch data. Public testimonials cannot fill this.
competitors_differentiation: CANS+ Balance is already a 330 ml magnesium/theanine/chamomile drink (1049 CZK/24 in same-day audit); Magnesia Antistress is lower-cost 700 ml; German Biolectra directly replaces pills. A lower-dose familiar-flavour drink may simplify use but has no established moat.
format_experience: one still or lightly sparkling portion, possibly a small bottle if pill-replacement proves the real job. Avoid choosing shot and full refreshment simultaneously.
promise_science_claims_classification: functional supplement drink. A 200–250 ml ordinary beverage with permitted nutrient forms is one possible route; a 25–60 ml explicit daily-dose shot is more plausibly a food supplement and needs separate national assessment. permitted magnesium claims concern normal psychological/nervous-system function and fatigue under conditions; they do not establish acute stress relief in magnesium-replete users. No clinically validated final product. Any botanical/theanine addition adds exact-preparation/legal questions rather than automatic differentiation.
repeat_pattern: an already chosen nutrient routine paired with taste, one portion/day if appropriate; repeat must not rely on feeling sedation or using several social servings.
price_channel_benchmarks: CANS+ ~43.71 CZK/can DTC versus inexpensive mineral water and tablets; pharmacy/drugstore/specialist route may fit a supplement, café/office route a beverage. Price for a new offer unknown.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: exact magnesium form, dose, stability, bitterness, bowel tolerance and total intake; no use of Biolectra's 300 mg as a formulation target. Claims and serving instructions must fit classification. Social multi-can consumption is poorly matched to concentrated daily doses.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: current alternatives may fully satisfy users; transport of water adds cost to an inexpensive nutrient; the popular “anti-stress” narrative may create an expectation the compliant product cannot meet.
invalidating_assumptions: customers want a fast felt effect; no reason to abandon pills/water; acceptable premium insufficient; desired doses create sensory/tolerance problems.
cheapest_next_validation: audit existing magnesium alternatives and conduct future task-based interviews with current supplement users, explicitly comparing the nutrition promise with neutral flavour/refreshment. No formula work until the non-sedating promise survives.
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: Existing liquid supplements; no switch premium/repeat
occasion_frequency_breadth: Daily routine hypothetical; broad need not established
competitive_defensibility: Cheap tablets/mineral water/liquid supplement already serve
regulatory_feasibility: Permitted Mg form ordinary beverage or separately assessed supplement
scientific_credibility: Normal nutrient function; not acute calm; dose/tolerance limits
assumption_dependence: High: meaningful routine substitution and willingness to pay
report_section: A caffeine-free nutrition drink for the afternoon pause, for existing magnesium-supplement users

name: A small bedtime bottle for adults who already choose a sleep supplement
proposition: a low-volume ready-to-drink bedtime dose for an existing supplement user who dislikes preparation or tablets.
target_customer_occasion_geography: occasional sleep-onset-support users, research first in France/Germany as separate regulatory and customer markets; not people seeking an insomnia treatment, not a social round, and not a recommendation for shift workers.
substitutes_unresolved_need: tablets, gummies, sprays, tea, routines and clinical care; alleged convenience gap unverified. Large bedtime drink volume itself may be undesirable.
need_evidence: French 2024 survey reports 33.1% insomnia complaints and 21.5% short sleepers; outcomes/geography are specific. The highest burden among financially strained adults argues against assuming premium affordability. [SPF](https://inpes.santepubliquefrance.fr/sommeil/donnees).
paid_demand_evidence: no credible local sleep-RTD repeat found; US mixed-format Dream Water results cannot supply it. Public demand for existing cheap dose forms is a substitute signal only.
competitors_differentiation: a mini bottle could remove preparation, but supplements already do. Historical Austrian Snoooze proves the format was tried, not why it disappeared or whether a current opportunity exists.
format_experience: 30–100 ml finished bottle, one explicit dose; no formula, dose or safe chronic pattern selected.
promise_science_claims_classification: functional supplement drink commercially; food supplement is more plausible than a casual social beverage, with national medicine-borderline assessment required. any melatonin route must fit an authorised claim's exact conditions plus national classification/safety restrictions; an EU claim does not authorise every product category/country. Botanical-only “sleep” cannot borrow clinical efficacy from different extracts. Never imply insomnia treatment.
repeat_pattern: occasional or course-based use according to a justified label, not automatic nightly subscription; lower repeat frequency weakens liquid economics.
price_channel_benchmarks: German dm lists melatonin tablets/gummies around cents per dose and many alternatives; no current comparable EU sleep-RTD price verified. Pharmacy/drugstore more credible than bar or office routes.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: melatonin national legal status, label warnings, interactions, stability/homogeneity, adult-only audience, no multi-serving use, no driving/social-relaxation conflation. Detailed official regulatory workstream controls this route.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: heavy need does not imply product fit; cheap pills/sprays solve convenience; ritual may require warm tea; sparse RTD supply can reflect poor demand and regulation. Snoooze absence is not evidence of failure.
invalidating_assumptions: no preparation/tablet dissatisfaction; purchasers mainly seek a medical claim; target country's route is unsuitable; only persistent/chronic use makes economics work.
cheapest_next_validation: country-specific classification/claim desk check first, then future interviews of existing adult supplement users about actual format dissatisfaction. No manufacturing unless both gates pass.
need_evidence_strength: Sleep burden strong; RTD-specific unmet need weak
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: No verified new shot demand/repeat; cheap substitutes
occasion_frequency_breadth: Appropriate use may be occasional; chronic repeat not safety evidence
regulatory_feasibility: High country divergence; CZ1 mg food route conflicts; NL classification conditional
scientific_credibility: Melatonin onset claim conditional; not sleep quality or long-term safety
manufacturing_capital: Dose accuracy, stability, classification and shot MOQ risk
channel_economics: Supplement channels fit in principle; access, economics unknown
assumption_dependence: Very high: legal category, dose, format need, safe pattern
report_section: A small bedtime bottle for adults who already choose a sleep supplement

name: An approachable compact protein drink for independently living older adults with an actual dietary shortfall
proposition: a modestly sized bottle delivering meaningful protein for people who demonstrably struggle to fit it into food, with everyday rather than bodybuilding presentation.
target_customer_occasion_geography: independently living older adults with an identified habitual intake problem; NL/FR research cells because evidence and relevant grocery alternatives exist. Daily snack/breakfast adjacency is a hypothesis.
substitutes_unresolved_need: milk, yogurt, quark, eggs/food, cheap protein RTDs, powders, medical nutrition when appropriate. Claimed gaps in taste, portion or identity have not been established for a defined segment.
need_evidence: INRAE describes age-related anabolic resistance and research on nutrition composition, but not blanket deficiency or need for a drink. Dutch 2010–12 consumption survey found protein sufficient for most sampled community-dwelling older adults; frail people were underrepresented. Dutch 2021 advice found no convincing/probable general benefit above its recommended intake in healthy older adults. [INRAE 2025](https://www.inrae.fr/actualites/jusquou-peut-vegetaliser-lalimentation-seniors-assurant-leurs-besoins-nutritionnels); [RIVM older-adult survey](https://www.rivm.nl/voedselconsumptiepeiling/overzicht-voedselconsumptiepeilingen/vcp-ouderen-70-jaar-en-ouder-2010-2012); [Dutch protein reference-values advice](https://www.gezondheidsraad.nl/site/binaries/site-content/collections/documents/2021/03/02/voedingsnormen-voor-eiwitten/Advies-Voedingsnormen-voor-eiwitten-referentiewaarden-voor-de-inname-van-eiwitten.pdf).
paid_demand_evidence: current protein RTD supply is strong; target-specific willingness to pay and incremental repeat unknown. Danone whole-range growth is not exact bottle demand.
competitors_differentiation: AH vanilla 250 ml/~20.75 g protein/€1.49; Danone 25 g drinkable dairy range. Everyday branding alone is easy to imitate. A genuine sensory/intake problem must be shown against these.
format_experience: 200–250 ml bottle, still, easy to open; no validated protein source, recipe or clinical effect. Ambient shelf stability is a desired dependency, not established capability.
promise_science_claims_classification: functional supplement drink commercially; ordinarily a conventional protein beverage. Any product for dietary management of disease/malnutrition may enter foods-for-special-medical-purposes requirements; do not use this as a shortcut into treatment. protein maintenance-of-muscle claim is scientifically more grounded than most exotic cognition blends, subject to legal conditions. It does not establish recovery, frailty prevention, sarcopenia treatment or benefit in already adequate diets.
repeat_pattern: replace a demonstrably missed protein-rich food occasion; avoid displacing sufficient meals. Actual routine and sustained acceptance unknown.
price_channel_benchmarks: €1.49 Dutch grocery bottle is a difficult reference; independent grocers/active-age groups or pharmacy distribution would require access and clear positioning, none secured.
manufacturing_regulatory_safety_dependen: protein quality, allergens, viscosity, sedimentation, aseptic/UHT or refrigeration, shelf life, filling MOQ, clinical-category boundary and target-population safety. More manufacturing complexity than a simple acidic drink.
counterevidence_gap_explanation: healthy older adults are not universally protein-deficient; cheap familiar products already work; marketing “for seniors” may deter rather than help; clinical needs bring a different business and evidence burden.
invalidating_assumptions: no meaningful shortfall; only a medical audience has need; existing bottle is acceptable; sensory or process requirements make price uncompetitive.
cheapest_next_validation: secondary-data segmentation plus a future comparison of existing bottles/foods among people with observed intake difficulty. No prototype before proving a product-specific deficit in alternatives.
need_evidence_strength: Protein role established; generic older-adult shortfall contradicted
paid_repeat_evidence_strength: Cheap existing bottles; target-specific paid demand unknown
occasion_frequency_breadth: Daily snack possible only if real shortfall
competitive_defensibility: AH250 ml 20.75 gEUR 1.49 strong comparator; age branding copyable
regulatory_feasibility: Ordinary protein food plausible; clinical targeting may requireFSMP
scientific_credibility: Protein maintenance credible; no universal deficit or treatment promise
channel_economics: Grocery/pharmacy access unknown; difficult low-price anchor
assumption_dependence: High: defined subgroup, intake gap, sensory advantage, manufacturing
recommendation: Reject generic age-based thesis; reopen only for documented subgroup
report_section: An approachable compact protein drink for independently living older adults with an actual dietary shortfall
